stories.headline: Trump ties Iran war deal to 'mandatory' Abraham Accords as Tehran says agreement 'not imminent'

key_facts.fact: On May 25, Trump posted on Truth Social that it should be 'mandatory' for Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt and Jordan to 'simultaneously' sign the Abraham Accords as part of efforts to reach a deal ending the war with Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: "After all the work done by the United States to try and pull this very complex puzzle together, it should be mandatory that all of these Countries, at a minimum, simultaneously, sign onto the Abraham Accords," Trump wrote in a lengthy social media post.

key_facts.fact: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqai said on Monday May 25 that the two sides had reached understandings on a large portion of issues, but that signing an agreement was 'not imminent'.
key_facts.excerpt: "It is correct to say that we have reached a conclusion on a large portion of the issues under discussion," Baqai said in Tehran on Monday. "But to say that this means the signing of an agreement is imminent - no-one can make such a claim."

key_facts.fact: The memorandum of understanding under discussion reportedly involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and a plan for further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme.
key_facts.excerpt: The memorandum of understanding reportedly involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and a plan for further negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme.

key_facts.fact: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a memorandum of understanding could materialize 'today', though the US would deal with Iran 'in another way' if a good deal was not reached.
key_facts.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that a memorandum of understanding to end the war with Iran could materialize "today," though if a "good deal" isn't reached, the US would deal with the country in "another way."

key_facts.fact: A fragile ceasefire has held since April 7-8 despite occasional drone and missile attacks; the US imposed a blockade of Iran's ports on April 17, which would be lifted in parallel with the strait gradually reopening under the emerging deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the emerging agreement, the strait would gradually reopen in parallel with the U.S. ending the blockade of Iran's ports it imposed on April 17, the regional officials said.

stories.headline: China restricts overseas travel for top AI researchers at Alibaba, DeepSeek

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Tuesday May 26 that China is restricting overseas travel for top AI professionals at private firms including Alibaba and DeepSeek, an escalation of measures to safeguard its technology and catch up to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: China is restricting overseas travel for top AI professionals in private firms such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and DeepSeek, suggesting an escalation in measures intended to safeguard its technology and catch up to the US in a pivotal sphere.

key_facts.fact: Government agencies have begun imposing restrictions on individuals involved in advanced AI work deemed strategically important; those people now need approval from relevant authorities before traveling abroad.
key_facts.excerpt: Government agencies have begun imposing restrictions on individuals involved in advanced AI work and considered strategically important to the country... That means they need approval from relevant authorities before embarking on overseas travel.

key_facts.fact: The measures extend long-standing travel curbs that China had previously imposed on key personnel to AI talent at private companies.
key_facts.excerpt: China is restricting overseas travel for top professionals involved in advanced and strategically important AI work at firms like Alibaba Group Holding and DeepSeek, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

sources.title: China Expands Travel Curbs to Top AI Talent at Private Firms

stories.headline: Iran's president orders reopening of international internet after 87-day blackout

key_facts.fact: On Monday May 25, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the Ministry of Communications to restore international internet access to its pre-January status, his spokesman said.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday ordered the Ministry of Communications to restore international internet access to its pre-January status, his spokesman said.

key_facts.fact: IRGC-affiliated Fars News questioned the administration's authority to issue the order, arguing the decision to restrict access was made by the Supreme National Security Council and must be reversed by the same body.
key_facts.excerpt: The IRGC-affiliated Fars News earlier questioned the administration's authority to issue such an order, arguing that the decision to restrict internet access was made by the Supreme National Security Council and must therefore be reversed by the same body.

key_facts.fact: Most Iranians had been unable to access the worldwide web for 87 days as of May 25, according to internet observatory NetBlocks, with only a few citizens using expensive VPNs to circumvent restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: Most Iranians have been unable to access the worldwide web for 87 days according to the internet observatory NetBlocks on May 25, with only a few citizens having access to expensive and advanced VPNs that circumvent the restrictions.

key_facts.fact: The blackout was reimposed after US and Israeli strikes against Iran began on February 28; an earlier blackout had been imposed from January 8 in response to anti-government protests.
key_facts.excerpt: Authorities initially imposed an internet blackout from Jan 8 in response to nationwide anti-government protests... before a new blackout was initiated following the start of US and Israeli strikes against Iran on Feb 28.

key_facts.fact: The order followed a fourth meeting of the Special Task Force on Cyberspace Management that ended with 9 votes in favor and 3 against reconnecting Iran to the global internet; ISNA said implementation was expected on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: The president's order came after the fourth meeting of the Special Task Force on Cyberspace Management ended with 9 votes in favor and 3 against reconnecting Iran to the global internet after more than 85 days of disruption.

stories.headline: Chongqing floods and landslides kill 9, leave 11 missing as record rain hits southwest China

key_facts.fact: Extreme rainfall and landslides in Chongqing's Yongchuan district killed nine people and left 11 missing, after rain struck late Saturday and early Sunday (May 23-24).
key_facts.excerpt: Extreme rainfall and resulting landslides in southwestern China's Chongqing municipality have killed nine people and left 11 missing.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 300mm of rain fell in two hours, the worst in over 60 years; 1,800 rescuers were deployed and 2,100 people evacuated.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 300mm of rain fell in 2 hours, the worst in over 60 years; 1,800 rescuers deployed, 2,100 evacuated.

key_facts.fact: The Chongqing Municipal Planning and Natural Resources authorities issued the first red alert for geological disaster risk of 2026, covering Fengjie and Wushan counties from 8am Monday to 8am Tuesday and identifying 41 villages at very high risk.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chongqing Municipal Planning and Natural Resources Observatory, along with the Chongqing Meteorological Observatory, issued the first red alert for geological disaster risk in 2026. From 8 am Monday to 8 am Tuesday, Fengjie and Wushan counties were placed under Level-I (red) warnings.

key_facts.fact: The China National Commission for Disaster Reduction activated a Level-IV emergency response, and the National Development and Reform Commission allocated 20 million yuan (about $2.93 million) from the central budget.
key_facts.excerpt: The China National Commission for Disaster Reduction on Sunday activated a Level-IV emergency response for floods and geological disasters in Chongqing.

stories.headline: Zelensky tells lawmakers Ukraine war could end by November with security guarantees

key_facts.fact: President Volodymyr Zelensky told his Servant of the People party on May 25 that hostilities could conclude by November if Kyiv receives robust security guarantees, lawmaker Olha Vasylevska-Smahliuk said.
key_facts.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told his Servant of the People party that hostilities in the Russo-Ukrainian war could conclude by November if Kyiv receives robust security guarantees, lawmaker Olha Vasylevska-Smahliuk said on May 25.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Europe was expected to name an official to help mediate a peace process and that a US delegation is due to arrive in Ukraine soon.
key_facts.excerpt: She added that Zelenskyy said Europe was expected to name an official to help mediate a peace process and that a U.S. delegation is due to arrive in Ukraine soon.

key_facts.fact: Vasylevska-Smahliuk said Ukraine has 'an advantage on the front that we can use' and that the main goal is to prevent Russia from launching a new offensive after a short pause.
key_facts.excerpt: "We now have an advantage on the front that we can use," she said... "The main goal is to prevent Russia from deceiving us and, after a short pause, launching new operations or a new offensive."

key_facts.fact: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on May 25 that Putin is trying to draw Europe into peace negotiations primarily to secure relief from sanctions, warning Europe against taking a mediator role.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin is trying to draw Europe into peace negotiations as a mediator primarily to secure relief from sanctions, Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said during a Ukraina stuudio broadcast on May 25.

stories.headline: FDA approves Taiho's oral Inqovi plus venetoclax for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Taiho Oncology's Inqovi (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax for adults with newly diagnosed AML who are 75 or older or ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Taiho Oncology's Inqovi (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax for the treatment of adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are 75 years or older or who are ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: The combination is the first and only oral hypomethylating regimen approved for this population, offering an alternative to injected agents that require frequent clinic visits.
key_facts.excerpt: The combination of Inqovi plus venetoclax is the first and only oral hypomethylating regimen approved for this population, offering an alternative to parenteral hypomethylating agent-based regimens that require frequent clinic visits.

key_facts.fact: Approval was based on the Phase II ASCERTAIN-V study, in which 42 patients (41.6%) achieved complete remission with a median time to CR of two months.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval was based on results from the Phase II ASCERTAIN-V study, which showed that the combination treatment resulted in 42 patients achieving a complete remission (CR; 41.6%), with a median time to CR of two months.

key_facts.fact: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 82% of patients, including febrile neutropenia (31%) and sepsis (22%); fatal adverse reactions occurred in 8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 82% of patients who received the combination treatment, including serious adverse reactions of febrile neutropenia (31%), sepsis (22%)... Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 8% of patients.

sources.title: FDA approves Inqovi for acute myeloid leukemia

stories.headline: Explosion threat at California aerospace chemical tank eliminated after 50,000 evacuated

key_facts.fact: Fire authorities said early Monday May 25 that the threat of a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE) at a chemical storage tank at GKN Aerospace in Garden Grove, California, had been eliminated, marking a turning point in the days-long emergency.
key_facts.excerpt: In a Monday morning update, firefighters said the threat of a boiling liquid expanding vapor explosion (BLEVE) has been eliminated, but evacuations remained in effect.

key_facts.fact: The crisis began Thursday night when a tank containing the flammable liquid methyl methacrylate overheated; about 50,000 people were placed under evacuation orders and Governor Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency.
key_facts.excerpt: About 50,000 people in the Orange County community were under evacuation orders, and Gov. Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency. Evacuations were reduced Monday afternoon.

key_facts.fact: A crack detected in the tank over the weekend allowed pressure to dissipate, easing the explosion risk; evacuations were reduced Monday afternoon.
key_facts.excerpt: A crack was detected in the tank over the weekend, which allowed pressure inside the tank to dissipate. Evacuations were reduced Monday afternoon.

sources.title: Garden Grove tank explosion threat reaches turning point
